'''David Colin Sherrington''' FRS (5 March 1945 – 4 October 2014) was a polymer chemist&nbsp;whose research career was based at the [[University of Strathclyde]].<ref name=roysoc>{{Cite journal|last1=Richards|first1=Randal W.|last2=Hodge|first2=Philip|date=2017|title=David Colin Sherrington. 5 March 1945—4 October 2014|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=64|pages=367–385|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2017.0021|s2cid=79823764|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Biography==
David Colin Sherrington was born at Webster Street, [[Litherland]], Liverpool on 5 March 1945, the second child of Alfred George Sherrington, a dock labourer, and Lucy Gladys Sherrington, née Pyke. He attended two primary/junior schools before passing the [[eleven-plus]] exam, enabling him to go to Waterloo Grammar School. [[Crosby, Merseyside|Crosby]]. His [[A-Level]] results were good enough for him to by-pass the first year of the chemistry degree course at the [[University of Liverpool]] and enter the second year in 1963. He graduated first-class in 1966.

Sherrington stayed at Liverpool for his PhD, under [[Anthony Ledwith]], and then continued as a research assistant in the same department so that he could help his recently widowed mother. In 1971 he applied for two fellowships: at [[Heriot-Watt University]] and at the [[University of Strathclyde]]. He was successful with the second, and took up a post in Alastair
M. North’s department of pure and applied chemistry.

Before moving north, David Sherrington married Valerie Vinnicombe at County Road Methodist Church, [[Walton, Liverpool|Walton]] in June 1972.<ref>{{cite news|title = June brides... |newspaper = The Liverpool Echo | date = 27 June 1972 | page = 2}}</ref> They had met at the university tennis club, where she was secretary and he was trying to lose weight.<ref name=roysoc/>

By 1975 his researches in Scotland had become focused on polymer-supported reactions.<ref>{{cite journal| last1 = Sherrington|first1 = D C|last2 = Craig|first2 = D J|last3 = Dalgliesh|first3 = J|last4 = Domin|first4 = G|last5 = Taylor | first5 = J|last6 = Meehan|first6 = G V|title = Highly crosslinked polymeric reagents. Polymer-supported phosphines and their use in the conversion of alcohols to chloroalkanes|journal =  European Polymer Journal|volume = 13|pages = 73–76|date = 1976 | issue=2 |doi=10.1016/0014-3057(77)90140-9}}</ref> In 1984 Sherrington accepted a three-year contract at [[Unilever Research & Development Port Sunlight Laboratory|Unilever’s Port Sunlight laboratory]] under its research director [[Geoffrey Allen (chemist)| Sir Geoffrey Allen, FRS]]. His job was to build and lead the Polymer Science Area. He worked in fields that had practical value – always his wish – such as [[Biodegradable polymer|biodegradable polymers]] and [[molecular imprinting]].<ref>{{cite journal| last1 = Wang|first1 = Jinfang| last2 = Cormack|first2=  Peter A G| last3 = Sherrington| first3= David C|last4= Khoshdel|first4= Ezat |title= Synthesis and characterization of micrometer-sized molecularly imprinted spherical polymer particulates prepared via precipitation polymerization | journal = Pure and Applied Chemistry |volume= 79|issue = 9| pages = 1505–1519 |date= 2007| doi=10.1351/pac200779091505 | s2cid=55051417 |doi-access= free}}</ref> Another area he developed was porpos polymers from high internal phase emulsions (PolyHIPEs), particularly as applied to [[solid phase peptide synthesis]].

Sherrington returned to Strathclyde in 1987 as a full professor and later the head of the organic chemistry section. His reputation grew and he was to hold visiting chairs in 10 universities around the world. He was awarded a DSc by his alma mater, and elected a Fellow of the Royal Societies of Edinburgh and London.

In their memoir of Sherrington Randal W. Richards and Philip Hodge note, that “It is very evident that David Sherrington made a major and unique impact on polymer science by enthusiastically bringing the rigour of physical chemistry to a new and rapidly expanding area of the subject and by being keen to collaborate with experts in other
Disciplines”.<ref name=roysoc/>

David Colin Carrington suffered from pain in his lower back for many years, and was finally diagnosed in April 2012 as having [[multiple system atrophy]] (MSA). He had two major attacks of pneumonia in 2014 and died on 4 October, survived by Val. They had no children.

Val has continued to raise awareness of MSA.<ref>{{cite news|last = Keenam| first = Amanda|title = Valerie Sherrington reveals how she turned to running to help her cope with the death of her husband from rare illness |newspaper = Daily Record  | date = 30 April 2015 | page = |url= https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/health/valerie-sherrington-reveals-how-turned-5608917| access-date = 12 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last = Sherrington| first = Valerie|title = David Colin Sherrington, FRS|website = JustGiving |url= https://www.justgiving.com/fundraising/valerie-sherrington| access-date = 12 May 2023}}</ref>
